thread:
anna: rolling out onyx13b-int4 checkpoint to canary. quick heads-up: 1) small quality dip on long-document summarization (~1.3 ROUGE-L) vs fp16 baseline; 2) sporadic latency tails and a few OOMs under concurrent batches >=5. sharing logs and my first-pass mitigations below.

mike: thanks — paste the OOM stack + the exact eval call you used? and what's the route defaults right now for this model?

anna: log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-20T21:08:11Z] ERROR runtime: cuda alloc failed: out of memory. free=142MiB requested=600MiB
stack: serve/runtime/allocator.go:324 serve/runtime/kv_cache.go:178
```
Eval I ran (local harness):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"onyx13b-int4","input":"Summarize: <very long doc>","max_new_tokens":512,"batch_size":6}'
```
Observed: median latency ~430ms, but p95 spikes around 1.1–1.3s; 4/150 requests hit OOM.

tariq: two fast mitigations: reduce max_new_tokens on the canary; and switch to a windowed batching mode with lower micro-batch cap. Also consider enabling kv trimming on slot pressure. Those should bound tail memory.

eva: about the quality drop — how was the PTQ done? per-channel? any outlier clipping? int4 variance can really affect summarization.

anna: current quant was symmetric 4-bit PTQ, 64-calib samples, no dedicated outlier handling. next steps: try (A) per-channel with outlier clipping (clip=2.5σ) and (B) bias-corrected rounding.

mike: suggested canary route update: 
```
route: onyx13b-int4-canary
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  batching:
    strategy: windowed
    micro_batch_cap: 3
    max_batch_tokens: 8192
  prefetch: off
  kv_eviction_threshold: 0.7
  session_max_len: 2048
  soft_throttle: 0.85
```
That should eliminate the observed OOMs and reduce p95.

ci-bot: ran a quick smoke against convo + summarization shards with those settings (500 requests):
- p50: 230ms (was ~430ms)
- p95: 480ms (was ~1.1s)
- OOMs: 0/500
- Summarization ROUGE-L delta: -1.1 vs fp16

tariq: good on perf. for model quality let's run the two PTQ variants A/B and compare on the full summarization eval (multiple seeds). Also add a mixed-shape perf run (short chats + long docs) to stress allocator fragmentation.

anna: kicking both variants now. eval commands: 
```
# variant A (per-channel + outlier clip)
python tools/eval.py --model onyx13b-int4-ptqA --tasks summarization --max_new_tokens 256 --batch 4
# variant B (bias-correct rounding)
python tools/eval.py --model onyx13b-int4-ptqB --tasks summarization --max_new_tokens 256 --batch 4
```
Also observed allocator behavior: on long contexts (>2k tokens) we see higher free/alloc churn and small free fragments left behind — int4 allocation alignment differs and may cause fragmentation leading to hard-to-reproduce OOMs.

mike: for runtime team: please file a ticket to add a compact-on-free pass or coalescing heuristic when fragmentation ratio > threshold. Short-term: enforce session_max_len=2048 for this model route.

ci-bot: first-pass results (18m):
- ptqA: ROUGE-L delta -0.4 vs fp16, p95 495ms
- ptqB: ROUGE-L delta -0.9 vs fp16, p95 470ms
Notes: ptqA (outlier-clipped per-channel) looks best for quality while perf is comparable.

eva: ptqA looks acceptable (<0.5 ROUGE-L drop). We should gate quant pipeline to fail or warn if delta > 1.0. Also add auto-eval in calibration.

tariq: agree. also add a perf regression test for small-short requests so we don't regress tiny-latency while fixing fragmentation.

anna: action items: 
- anna: promote ptqA to canary checkpoint and deploy with mike's route defaults (max_new_tokens=256, windowed batching, micro_batch_cap=3)
- mike: patch route to add soft_throttle and session_max_len override, will schedule canary at 5%
- tariq: open eng-runtime issue for allocator compaction heuristic and tag runtime owners
- eva: add quant-eval gating in calibration pipeline (fail if ROUGE-L delta > 1.0)

mike: scheduling canary tomorrow 09:30 PST at 5% traffic. @oncall please monitor.
